articles.title: The row over Rutland: can England’s smallest county survive?
articles.summary: Its council is due to merge with Leicestershire’s in 2028, and some locals are incensed. Can the county hold on to its ceremonial status – and biggest selling point? Mysterious disappearances have been taking place lately in Rutland, an East Midlands pocket between Leicestershire, Lincolnshire and…
body: The area’s MP, the Conservative Alicia Kearns, is “not sure” what the motivation behind the thefts is. But they are certainly a fitting metaphor for Rutland’s disappearing status: its council is due to merge with Leicestershire county council in spring 2028.

“The joke goes: ‘Rutland is England 50 years ago,’” says Kearns when we meet at the county’s most famous landmark, the UK’s largest reservoir by surface area, Rutland Water, home to the Rutland Osprey Project. She tells me about the county’s farming community, its tradition of Friday shoots that supply the local pubs with game, its pride in local businesses. So resistant are Rutlanders to some aspects of modernity, “we were the last county to have a McDonald’s built”, she says. Even when it did finally arrive, in 2020, the decision “was really controversial”.

articles.title: My pup Koopa and I put 15 dog beds to the test – these are ones that survived
articles.summary: We tried models from Black Lab, K9 Ballistics, Orvis, Znooz and others to find beds that were long-lasting, washable, and most of all, comfortable. The best dog harnesses and dog toys – pup-tested. Sign up for the Filter US newsletter, your weekly guide to buying fewer, better things.
body: While our four-legged best friends are often happy enough to sprawl on the floor or curl up on an old blanket, there’s an increasing number of companies out there making plush and durable spots for pampered pups to lie.

But given the destructive tendencies of some dogs and that some of these beds cost well into the hundreds of dollars, buying the wrong one can quickly turn into an expensive mess. We tested 15 different models to find the best for every situation.

I’ve tested everything from sports cars to smartphones for dozens of international outlets since the late 90s, but I’ve been a dog owner and lover my entire life. For the Filter, my pups and I have put dog harnesses and dog toys to the test. Along the way, my pups have curled up on everything from leftover couch cushions to high-grade beds from big-brand stores.
I’ve seen which types of beds work and which fall apart, which are easy to take apart and which are a real struggle and which stand up best to repeated cleaning and drying cycles.

articles.title: People’s bodies are changing in the age of Ozempic. How are we meant to talk about it?
articles.summary: Discussing people’s bodies can be fraught. We asked eating disorder experts how to do so – or not – responsibly. In the age of Ozempic and people being open about plastic surgery, discussion about people’s bodies is rife.
body: It is a fraught topic. We asked eating disorder experts for guidelines to follow when talking about other people’s bodies, and how to do so without doing harm.

For experts in the field of eating disorders, the current ambivalence makes sense. “There’s a whiplash moment we’re stuck in,” says Dr Tom Hildebrandt, director of the Center for Eating and Weight Disorders at Mount Sinai hospital in New York.

The body positivity movement of the 2010s saw a mainstream push to “accept all body sizes, shapes and types”, says Hildebrandt. Then, with the explosion of GLP-1s, progress toward body acceptance “took a hard right turn”, he says – once again, “the media went through its idealization of weight loss”.
The vocabulary is different than it was before. Now, the focus is on “optimizing” one’s body and appearance, says Dr Ulrike Schmidt, professor of eating disorders at King’s College London.
points: In the age of Ozempic and people being open about plastic surgery, discussion about people’s bodies is rife.

articles.title: I’ve been told to apply to a civil and administrative tribunal over my faulty dishwasher. What does it involve?
articles.summary: Taking a consumer complaint to tribunal is likely to be onerous, writes policy professional Kat George, but the payoff may be worthwhile. A little over two years ago, I bought a new dishwasher. From the beginning, it did not function properly.
body: The retailer refused to accept a return for a refund or replacement, and because I bought it for my tenant, I had to replace it at my own cost. The whole process has been very frustrating, and I now have a useless dishwasher stored in my home, which remains under the manufacturer’s warranty.

I submitted a complaint to Fair Trading in a bid to force the retailer to engage with the issue, however the outcome was the same. Fair Trading says my next step is to apply to the NSW Civil and Administrative Tribunal (Ncat), if I am eligible. My question is: what would applying to Ncat involve? Could it lead to further costs for me?

Kat says: This is an extraordinarily frustrating situation. Under the Australian Consumer Law, however, you may have a strong argument that the dishwasher’s performance breaches the consumer guarantees.

articles.title: How to Party Like a Local in Mykonos, According to a Seasoned Veteran
articles.summary: A lifelong regular’s guide to choosing the right coast, landing in the part of the venue you meant to book, and getting home before the taxis disappear.
body: The sun starts to set on Little Venice and its windmills in Mykonos Town, one of many popular vistas on the island.

Now craft beer is brewed on the island, and casual Chora bars pour proper cocktails into paper cups and send revelers off into the night. Greek musicians share the calendar with international DJs, periodically reminding Mykonos of which country it belongs to. The familiar bottle-service caricature leaves out the drag stages of the old port and the smaller rooms where a night can change direction without a reservation. Prices remain high and the roads maddening, but few Mediterranean islands offer so many convincing ways to reach sunrise. After enough summers on both sides of the nap, I have settled on seven rules that every visitor needs to know.
Many of the outdoor tables in Little Venice are just inches from the tide.

articles.title: Roger Federer Reflects on His Hall-of-Fame Career
articles.summary: Ahead of a starry exhibition match at Arthur Ashe, Federer chats with Vogue about his Tennis Hall of Fame induction, his own estimation of his legendary career, the state of tennis today.
body: When I roll up to the flagship of On, the Swiss shoe company, in Manhattan’s Flatiron neighborhood, I find scores of schoolkids queued up outside. Many are holding tennis rackets and tennis balls with the dream of having them signed by the man many call the greatest to ever play the game: Roger Federer.

The newest inductee to the International Tennis Hall of Fame (alongside broadcaster Mary Carillo)—the festivities are this coming weekend in Newport, Rhode Island—he has been all over New York in the last few days, launching a limited-edition version of On’s The Roger shoe (with a grass-colored sockliner and some intriguing Easter eggs that we’ll let you discover on your own) and attracting another huge throng of fans yesterday at Arthur Ashe Stadium, merely to witness him warming up on the court with Lorenzo Musetti.

Vogue: Before we get into the Hall of Fame and talk about the exhibition, I wanted to ask you about your so-called retirement. Do you feel retired? Is your life different now? You seem pretty busy to me.

articles.title: 6 Fall Denim Trends to Shop Now, According to Experts
articles.summary: Are skinny jeans back? Is low-rise here to stay? From Agolde to Frame to Ossou, we tapped experts to weigh in on the top fall denim trends of 2026.
body: Although a seasonless category, denim is a serious power player in the fall capsule wardrobe, serving as outfit building blocks as the cooler temperatures hit. New jeans are always a smart buy as you start transitioning your wardrobe to greet the shift in season. And although we’ve seen plenty of trends emerge over the past year, fall 2026 denim trends carry several spring themes forward, from bootcut to deep indigo washes to colored denim. However, the pendulum is beginning to swing: Slouchier wide-leg proportions of the past are making room for streamlined silhouettes, with straight-leg and slim cigarette styles coming back into focus.

With a little help from the experts at some of the most beloved denim brands —Levi’s, Citizens of Humanity, Still Here, and Agolde, to name a few—we’re unpacking the jean styles you should be investing in for fall 2026. Spoiler alert: Many of them are bona fide closet classics, which means they won’t feel too out of touch with the pairs you might already hold near and dear.

articles.title: This Ultra-Wide Samsung Gaming Monitor Is $650 Off (and Comes With a $120 Amazon Gift Card)
articles.summary: We may earn a commission from links on this page. Deal pricing and availability subject to change after time of publication. An ultra-wide curved gaming monitor with ridiculous specs is every gamer's dream, but they (usually) don't come cheap.
body: The Samsung Odyssey Neo G9 Series is not a regular ultra-wide gaming monitor. It has impressive specs, but you'll need a top-notch gaming computer with specific outputs to take full advantage of its 240Hz refresh rate potential.

This monitor came out in 2023 with an "excellent" review from PCMag, mainly due to its impressive 7,680 by 2,160 4K native resolution, the ridiculous 57-inch screen size, its great color range and accuracy, the 240Hz refresh rate, and its design. The VA panel also means you get a bright 1,000-nit screen. To make full use of its powerful 240Hz refresh rate, you'll need to use a DisplayPort 2.1, or you'll be limited to 120Hz. You'll also need a powerful modern graphics card that is able to push the frames at a native resolution to max out the monitor's potential.

Although it is pricey, this monitor is a great value for the right gamer. You'll need plenty of space to fit a 57-inch screen, as well as a powerful computer to justify using the monitor—if you're not a competitive gamer with a powerful computer, it's probably not worth the price tag. Instead, consider this Asus gaming monitor going for $449.99 (originally $499) right now.

articles.title: 9 Best Collagen Creams Work Overtime to Plump and Firm Skin
articles.summary: Do collagen creams really work? Nine doctors weigh in, revealing everything you need to know about choosing a collagen cream for a more youthful complexion.
body: Here’s the juicy truth about anti-aging skincare: Prioritizing moisture can help the skin maintain a firm, bouncy appearance long after collagen levels start to decline. And the best collagen creams—which can moisturize, boost collagen production, and protect existing collagen—go a long way to make up for lost proteins.

To find the right collagen cream for your routine, consider your goals. “For a quick hydration boost, opt for formulas with collagen,” Valerie Aparovich, a biochemist, certified cosmetologist-aesthetician, and the science team lead at OnSkin, instructs. While hydration alone can plump and boost radiance, firming and wrinkle reduction call for ingredients—like peptides and exosomes—that can penetrate the surface of the skin to stimulate collagen production in the dermal layers. And when it comes to preserving existing collagen, antioxidants are key.

And with that key to collagen creams, you’re ready to shop! Ahead, find an edit of the best of them, whether you’re in the market for a buzzy K-beauty find, a high-tech formulation, or the Elemis cream that started it all.

articles.title: From the Archives: Good Golly Miss Dolly Parton
articles.summary: Country icon Dolly Parton has died at age 80, according to a statement from her family. To celebrate her exuberant life and work, we’re revisiting a 1994 profile of Parton by Charles Gandee.
body: The singer-songwriter, author, actor, and philanthropist Dolly Parton has died at age 80, according to a statement from her family. To celebrate her exuberant life and work, we’re revisiting a 1994 profile of Parton—described as an “improbable American icon”—by Charles Gandee.
“Good Golly Miss Dolly” by Charles Gandee was published in the January 1994 issue of Vogue.

The inspiration for Parton’s precocious preoccupation? “When I was little, I didn’t know what a whore meant or a tramp. But there were these three women in town, and I thought they were beautiful. Especially this one. She had this beautiful blond hair, red fingernails, high-heeled shoes, and hose with the seam up the back. And she’d walk the streets every Saturday. And then the guys would pick her up. And in my mind, as a little kid, that’s how I wanted to look. I have always said that honestly and truly I have patterned my look after the town tramp.”
points: Country icon Dolly Parton has died at age 80, according to a statement from her family.
